headline: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said Pakistan plans to require social media platforms to register with a new regulator and appoint representatives, saying only 47% of counter-terrorism departments' requests are acted upon, Arab News reports.

card.desc: Naqvi: only 47% of counter-terrorism requests acted upon

caption:
Pakistan plans to make social media platforms register! 📱
According to Arab News, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Tuesday that Pakistan plans to require social media companies to register with a new regulator and appoint representatives to deal with Pakistani authorities. Speaking at a Sustainable Development Policy Institute seminar in Islamabad, attended by representatives of Meta and TikTok, he said only 47% of requests from counter-terrorism departments are acted upon by the platforms. Registration would also apply to streaming services and major content creators; no deadline was given. "Blocking a whole platform will remain a last resort," Naqvi said.
